facts.heading: Anxiety worsens in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it gets worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school. She has taught at the school for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years and i love it.

facts.heading: Head asked to step up
facts.content: The head asked Hannah to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: the head asked me to step up when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being noticed
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking someone will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: and that sooner or later someone will notice i have no idea what i'm doing.

facts.heading: Rehearsing in mind
facts.content: Hannah rehearses in her head on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and i start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses possible questions and what she would say.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what i would say and what they would think of me if i got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they give the job to a nice year for a teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves' treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah. He told her he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be capable.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if i'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares her work to her mother's career.
facts.evidence: Everything i do, i think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother was a head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy in village
facts.content: People in the village still praise Hannah's mother as a wonderful head.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me and say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement and library
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago, and a library is named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's supportive comments
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says i've always worried too much and i should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hiding how bad it is
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad her feelings are.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like i'm making a fuss, so i don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to worries
facts.content: Hannah is awake due to various worries such as timetable changes and a parent complaint.
facts.evidence: Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round.

facts.heading: Increased coffee consumption
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day since the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term, I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Covering up physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah splashed her face with water during a meeting last Thursday because she felt unwell.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice reaction
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when her partner Ben suggests she should just enjoy things.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, he fits it.

facts.heading: Loss of school friends
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school and finds it awkward now.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4th quarter with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Lost company along with promotion
facts.content: Hannah lost some company along with her promotion.
facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that.

facts.heading: Missing school environment
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and the daily experience of children getting something for the first time.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Missing class and friends
facts.content: Hannah misses her class and her former friends.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Desire for promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and said yes because she couldn't say no to the head.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Crying after promotion decision
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Tears about not returning
facts.content: Hannah cried about not getting to go back to the previous situation.
facts.evidence: A year I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for 10 days.

facts.heading: Relaxation during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of Hannah.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Pre-term distress
facts.content: Hannah was a wreck the week before term and could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a chill laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it. She felt like she was bragging to herself.
facts.evidence: I stopped because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.

facts.heading: Goal to avoid feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves not rehearsing in meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening rest
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa without her stomach being in knots on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling after stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt a light fall and lighter when stating her goals out loud. She also felt a bit tearful.
facts.evidence: A light fall. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Difficulty telling Ben about issue
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are, not even Ben. She has not told Ben about the 4am issue.
facts.evidence: Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Considering telling Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah is considering telling Ben about the issue this week. She might choose a quiet moment on Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: I suppose I might try this week. If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up. Saturday morning, perhaps? He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Intention to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah intends to try the evening notebook again for a week, even just one line. She plans to put it by the kettle.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again just for a week? Even one line? I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Regret about cancelled line
facts.content: Hannah mentioned one line she nearly cancelled this morning. She expressed gladness about not cancelling it.
facts.evidence: One line that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't. I'm glad too.
